subject: Clarify LLM opt-out / prompt & response ownership + export paths
messages:
From: Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@novamed.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify model-improvement opt-out + prompt/response ownership

Hi Marcus / Priyom,

Thanks for the call earlier. A couple of follow-ups from NovaMed legal and product:

- We need a binding "no-training" (no-model-improvement) commitment for our tenant data. Can Redwood turn on a customer-level flag that prevents any training or model updates using our prompts/responses?
- Are prompts and generated responses treated as customer IP (we want rights to use and export them) or does Redwood reserve derivative rights for telemetry/aggregation use?
- Operationally, we need a reliable export path for transcripts and logs (SFTP or API) on a daily cadence, and an SLA for export availability.
- Please also confirm whether subprocessors in India/EU will see raw transcripts and whether those transfers are logged/auditable.

Can you send a short implementation plan and sample language we can circulate to our procurement/legal team?

Thanks,
Sana
Sana Gupta
Head of Data Product, NovaMed Health

--
(Attachment: nova-contract-summary.pdf - summary of existing procurement asks)

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@novamed.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify model-improvement opt-out + prompt/response ownership

Hi Sana — thanks, will outline specifics below and attach a one‑page DPA summary. High level answers first:

- No‑training flag: yes — we can enable a tenant opt‑out from model improvement. That flag ensures inference requests are marked, excluded from both short‑term telemetry and any offline training pipelines.
- Ownership: prompts and responses remain customer data. Redwood will not assert derivative ownership for customer content when the no‑training flag is enabled. We may still collect telemetry (latency, token counts) in aggregated, non‑reversible form for platform health unless you request opt‑out of telemetry too.
- Export path & SLA: we support daily automated SFTP exports or API pulls. Typical export SLA is 99.9% availability for delivery windows; we can propose a dedicated daily window and retention policy in the export SLA draft.
- Subprocessors/transfers: we will provide the current subprocessor inventory and a per‑export audit log. Subprocessors that handle raw transcripts are limited to specific regions; transfers are logged and traceable.

Attached: redwood-dpa-exec-summary.pdf (one‑pager for procurement).

Next steps: Priyom will propose legal language for contract redlines and Hannah will map the ops implementation (routing, SFTP config, audit trail). I’ll follow up with a consolidated plan and a slot for a technical runbook review.

— Marcus Lin
Director, Product — Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood-dpa-exec-summary.pdf)

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@novamed.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify model-improvement opt-out + prompt/response ownership

Hi Sana — looping in legal detail. Key points for contract language and implementation:

- Contract language: we can add a DPA addendum clause: "Customer may enable a No‑Model‑Improvement flag which prohibits Redwood from using Customer Content for model training or model improvement; Redwood shall not assert derivative rights over Customer Content when this flag is enabled." I’ll provide redline text in the next email.

- Telemetry vs. content: we differentiate PII/PHI content (never retained past ephemeral KV TTL when requested) from platform telemetry (token counts, latency). If NovaMed requires, we can disable collection of telemetry at tenant level, but that may affect some observability features and cost optimization suggestions.

- Subprocessor handling: our current "raw transcript" subprocessors are located in: US (primary), EU (replication only), and India (ops for SFTP processing). We can implement onshore routing (US only) for NovaMed as part of a Dedicated or Private plan; for hosted customers we offer export-only access with onshore processing where required.

- Export mechanics: recommended path is daily SFTP push to NovaMed with an immutability manifest and HMAC verification. We can also provide API bulk export with incremental delta tokens. I’ve attached the subprocessor inventory and a draft export SLA for your review.

Attachments: subprocessor-inventory.csv, export-sla-draft.docx

Legal redlines I’ll circulate tomorrow. If you need an escrow for transcripts or additional IP guarantees we can scope that as an addendum (e.g., limited-use escrow for audit/legal hold).

— Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena@novamed.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify model-improvement opt-out + prompt/response ownership

Thanks — a few items from NovaMed legal after an initial pass:

1) Redlines: please provide the proposed DPA addendum text you referenced. We’ll circulate to procurement and will likely request a standard clause: confirmation that "no‑training" is technically enforced and demonstrable (audit logs).

2) Evidence of deletion: we need to see proof-of-deletion workflows and exported audit logs showing removal from staging caches and KV stores within X hours of a deletion request. Can Redwood produce an example audit extract?

3) Derivatives: we accept aggregated/non‑reversible telemetry for platform health, but not for model improvement. Please confirm that aggregated telemetry will never be used to improve models.

4) SOC2 / compliance: can Redwood provide SOC 2 Type II report and indicate whether subprocessors are covered under scope?

5) Emergency access / legal holds: in situations where NovaMed receives lawful process requiring access to transcripts, what is Redwood’s process for notification and preservation?

If you can return a draft addendum plus a short ops playbook (1–2 pages) covering exports/deletion/audit within 48 hours, procurement can move forward.

— Elena Rossi
General Counsel, NovaMed Health

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@novamed.com>, Sana Gupta <sana.gupta@novamed.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify model-improvement opt-out + prompt/response ownership

Elena / Sana — appreciate the detailed asks. Action plan and deliverables:

1) Contract draft: Priyom will circulate a DPA addendum redline today that includes the No‑Model‑Improvement clause, explicit "no derivative rights" language, and logging commitments. (Related link: DocuSign draft: https://redwood.app/docusign/ND-4782-signature)

2) Ops playbook: Hannah will publish a 2‑page runbook that shows the end‑to‑end flow for enablement of the no‑training flag, SFTP export configuration, audit log format (sample JSON line), and proof‑of‑deletion timeline (we commit to removing transient KV within 24 hours and recording the deletion event). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-exp-sla

3) Evidence & SOC2: we will provide a sample audit extract (redacted), and our SOC 2 Type II report (or the auditor contact for an NDA exchange).

4) Subprocessor/onshore routing: for NovaMed we propose US‑only routing for raw transcripts as part of an export‑only configuration; we’ll document subprocessors in the addendum.

5) Emergency / legal holds: we will follow standard notice procedures and preservation workflows; we’ll add the preservation escalation flow to the ops playbook.

I’ll schedule a 30‑minute handoff call with your procurement team Thursday morning to walk the draft SLA and runbook. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ND-4782

Thanks — expect the redline and runbook shortly.

— Marcus Lin
Director, Product — Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
(Internal: next steps in HubSpot deal ND-4782)
